$comment: Machine-readable navigation contract for every Core Hub client (web, desktop, android, ios). docs/clients/NAVIGATION.md explains it; scripts/navigation-check.mjs validates it; each client's parity test reads it.

destinations.title: new_chat
destinations.note: Opens a draft session and closes the menu.

destinations.title: search
destinations.note: A search sheet over sessions with the field focused; not History. A result from the global agent opens global_agent.

destinations.title: device_connections
destinations.note: Tab devices lists the person's own devices (rename, revoke, last seen, push); an admin sees everyone's and the push senders (contract decision §66, 2026-09-25). A Settings page since 2026-09-22: configured once, so not in the sidebar.

destinations.title: agent_manager
destinations.note: The agent cards: the registry from the server. A main-sidebar entry directly above Tasks since 2026-09-24 (owner: putting agents inside Settings was a design mistake). Each card's chips and its Settings button open that agent's pages directly. Owners and admins only.

destinations.title: models
destinations.note: Providers, keys and voice providers live here, never in a Settings tab. Its own Settings page since 2026-09-22.

destinations.title: knowledge
destinations.note: Journal, notes/memory browser, files, search (Phase 4). A Settings page since 2026-09-22.

destinations.title: chat
destinations.note: Session list: pinned, recent with counter, a search field and an active/archived/all filter carried in the URL (?sessions=). This list is the history; there is no separate History screen (owner decision, 2026-09-22).

destinations.title: tasks
destinations.note: Projects and tasks (kanban-style columns) with agent assignment. The section is named Tasks everywhere (owner decision 2026-09-21).

destinations.title: schedules
destinations.note: Cron jobs and workflows with status badges.

destinations.title: settings
destinations.note: One screen with tabs and a Tools section; no settings inside settings.

destinations.title: display
destinations.note: Connection mode, link target, input behaviour while busy, theme and background from the server, app language, text size.

destinations.title: this_device
destinations.note: Hub connection, voice input mode, dictation language, spoken replies, self-update where the platform allows it.

destinations.title: logs
destinations.note: The hub's and every Hermes gateway's own lines (DECISIONS §51): owners and admins only.

destinations.title: usage
destinations.note: Tokens and costs.

destinations.title: skills_usage
destinations.note: Which skills the agents loaded, and which never (contract decision §50).

destinations.title: performance
destinations.note: Runtime processes and snapshots.

destinations.title: theme
destinations.note: Theme and background. The footer theme chip is a local preference, not an entry.

destinations.title: workspaces
destinations.note: Manage workspaces (ADR 0005). The footer workspace chip only switches the X-Hub-Profile scope.

destinations.title: files
destinations.note: The selected profile's working folder (${DATA_DIR}/workspaces/<profile>): browse, upload, download, zip, new folder, rename, move, copy, delete, preview, edit text, attach to a chat. A file manager only — no shell, no commands (DECISIONS §65). Owner and admin; follows the top-bar profile chip.

destinations.title: terminal
destinations.note: A shell on the hub's host (DECISIONS §70). The owner only — not admins (owner, 2026-09-25) — and only while the hub runs with COREHUB_WEB_TERMINAL=1: a client shows the entry only when GET /terminal answers 200.

destinations.title: config_files
destinations.note: A coding agent's own instructions and settings files (CLAUDE.md, settings.json, AGENTS.md, config.toml …), one set for every profile in the home of the user the hub runs as (DECISIONS §77). Owners and admins; not on the phones.

destinations.title: agent_settings
destinations.note: Always last. Tabs come from the adapter's settings descriptor (ADR 0002). Shown for every agent the card offers a Settings button for (an installed one), whether or not it lists `settings` among its capabilities.

destinations.title: global_agent
destinations.note: No menu entry; reached from search results and the pending-actions bar (a top-bar button, not a destination). The person's one standing conversation in the profile, left out of the chats list (DECISIONS §46).

topBarChips.$comment: Not destinations: they switch state in place and never navigate. On web and desktop the profile is switched here, at the top of every screen (owner, 2026-09-24); the footer does not repeat it. Phones: place not decided yet — the owner does not want a permanent top bar eating the chat or task space there.

footerChips.$comment: Not destinations: they switch state in place and never navigate. The model is chosen in the composer and on Models, not here (owner, 2026-09-24).
footerChips.language: UI language (ar/en); content direction is per message.
footerChips.theme: Local preference mirrored by the Theme tool.

preAuth.$comment: Screens a client shows before anyone is signed in. They are not destinations: they have no entry anywhere in the navigation, cannot be reached from a signed-in session, and are not counted by the parity rules for rail/segments/footer. `title` is a key in `terms`; `routes` is per surface like `surfaceRoutes`. `setup` exists only while the hub has no owner account (ADR 0011); `login` is the way in afterwards.

profileScope.$comment: Profiles on each page (ADR 0016, owner 2026-09-24). Not destinations. `selector`: the top profile selector (topBarChips.workspace once the footer chip moves to the top bar) is always one concrete profile — the one the person is in; the app opens on it, new chats are made in it, per-profile configuration pages edit it; it never offers `All` and never filters a list. `listFilter`: the chats list's own filter, `All profiles` (the default on every entry into the app) or one profile; hidden for someone with one profile; it and the selector never move each other. `alwaysAll`: pages that always show every profile the person may enter (the hub decides which), with no profile filter at all — search, tasks and schedules (stage 2: a new task or schedule is made in the selector's profile; acting on an existing one uses the item's own profile). Items on a list that shows more than one profile carry a badge of their profile, and open in their own profile without moving the selector.

surfaceRoutes.$comment: Per-surface URL (web) or screen id of every destination that exists on that surface. A destination whose `surfaces` exclude the surface must be absent here; every other destination must be present. The web parity test (packages/web/tests/navigation.parity.test.ts) builds its router from this map.

desktop.$comment: The desktop app draws the web client (ADR 0009, ADR 0020), so it takes every web route that exists on the desktop and adds its own. `$extends` names the surface whose routes are inherited; nav:check resolves it the same way the client does.

agentShell.$comment: Inside an agent's pages the sidebar becomes that agent's list, the way Settings does (owner, 2026-09-24): a `back` row to the Agents page, then the agent's name and mark, then its `agentLevel` entries in order, only those its adapter declares. The rail and the segments step aside; the top-bar profile chip stays, because skills, MCP, memory and channels are per profile. Phones: the list is the page, and an opened page shows the way back.

legacyRoutes.$comment: Old URLs a client must still honour by redirecting. Each key is a path prefix on that surface that no destination uses any more; its value is the prefix it now lives under. The rest of the path is kept.
